Key Research Thinking Patterns: Data-Driven Spatial Risk Modeling: Utilizing geospatial coordinate mapping and kernel density estimation on Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS) data to identify blackspots and optimize resource allocation for roadway improvements.

Latency-Throughput Trade-off Optimization: Implementing runahead execution techniques, such as In-Order Runahead with Result Use (IORARU), to mask long-latency cache misses and mitigate the memory wall in x86 64-bit processor architectures.

Adaptive Multimedia Stream Management: Applying adaptive frame dropping and replication strategies alongside H.264/AVC encoding optimization to maintain video quality metrics (PSNR, SSIM) under variable network conditions in Wide Area Network Emulator (WANem) simulations.

Hardware-Software Co-Design for Situational Awareness: Integrating Controller Area Network (CAN) bus message translation with real-time hazard alerting algorithms to enable dynamic traffic signal control and driver alerting for severe weather conditions.
Summary Description: Ronald D. Barnes is a researcher at the University of Oklahoma specializing in the intersection of intelligent transportation systems and high-performance computer architecture. His work bridges macro-level safety planning, utilizing FARS data and geospatial analysis to enhance highway safety, with micro-level hardware innovations. He designs power-efficient multiprocessor systems, employing runahead execution and shared context units to overcome memory latency bottlenecks. Concurrently, he develops connected vehicle technologies, leveraging CAN bus data and DSRC networks to create real-time hazard alerting systems and adaptive video distribution strategies for adverse weather conditions. His research integrates theoretical algorithmic design with practical, hardware-aware implementations to improve critical infrastructure reliability and vehicular situational awareness.
